headline: US equity futures point to a lower open as tech-heavy Nasdaq lags amid Middle East-driven oil gains and AI growth concerns
raw_text:
- S&P 500 Futures (@ES) fall 0.70%, Dow Jones Futures (@YM) decline 0.23%, Nasdaq 100 Futures (@NQ) drop 1.61%, and Russell 2000 Futures (@ER2) edge lower 0.41%, signaling a gap-down open.
- Pre-market small-cap movers include TNON (TNON) declining about 11%, ACVA (ACVA) trading roughly flat, AENT (AENT) falling around 10%, and FTFT (FTFT) down about 10%.
- On the downside, GAUZ (GAUZ) trades flat pre-market, while ZUMZ (ZUMZ) trades flat and PMTS (PMTS) edges higher after recent earnings misses.
- Overnight earnings reports from Hain Celestial (HAIN) and Coda Octopus (CODA) arrive before the bell with limited initial price reaction noted.
- Asian markets trade mostly lower, with Japan’s Nikkei (@NKD) down around 0.8-1% and South Korea’s Kospi off 2.5-3.5% on AI slowdown concerns weighing on SoftBank and regional chip stocks.
- European indices are mixed, with Euronext and Deutsche Boerse advancing on revived merger talks between the two exchanges.
- Oil prices gain over 3%, with WTI (@CL) near $103 and Brent (@QA) around $107, as a Saudi pipeline closure and regional attacks heighten supply risks, while gold (@GC) prices slip.
- Today’s economic calendar is light, with no major US data releases scheduled, while Canadian CPI data is due.
